lines.text: Take a string thirty-six units long, and bend it into a triangle.
lines.caption: Take a string thirty-six units long, and bend it into a triangle.

lines.text: How many different shapes can you make?
lines.caption: How many different shapes can you make?

lines.text: Watch out: some tries go flat, and some repeat a side!
lines.caption: Watch out: some tries go flat, and some repeat a side!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count them without missing any.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count them without missing any.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: How many triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of thirty-six,
lines.caption: How many triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of thirty-six,

lines.text: and have three different side lengths?
lines.caption: and have three different side lengths?

lines.text: Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices.

lines.text: The three sides must add to thirty-six. For example, ten, twelve and fourteen.
lines.caption: The three sides must add to thirty-six. For example, ten, twelve and fourteen.

lines.text: All three must be different, so twelve, twelve, twelve doesn't count.
lines.caption: All three must be different, so twelve, twelve, twelve doesn't count.

lines.text: And the same three sides in a different order make the same triangle. We count it once.
lines.caption: And the same three sides in a different order make the same triangle. We count it once.

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: list by the longest side

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's make an organized list. Write each triangle smallest side first.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's make an organized list. Write each triangle smallest side first.

lines.text: Here's the triangle rule. The two shorter sides must add to MORE than the longest side.
lines.caption: Here's the triangle rule. The two shorter sides must add to MORE than the longest side.

lines.text: The shorter two make thirty-six minus the longest. So the longest side must be less than eighteen.
lines.caption: The shorter two make thirty-six minus the longest. So the longest side must be less than eighteen.

lines.text: And the longest side is at least a third of thirty-six. That's twelve.
lines.caption: And the longest side is at least a third of thirty-six. That's twelve.

lines.text: So the longest side is somewhere from twelve to seventeen.
lines.caption: So the longest side is somewhere from twelve to seventeen.

lines.text: Longest side seventeen: the other two add to nineteen.
lines.caption: Longest side seventeen: the other two add to nineteen.

lines.text: From three and sixteen up to nine and ten. That's seven.
lines.caption: From three and sixteen up to nine and ten. That's seven.

lines.text: The middle side has to stay below seventeen, and the smallest below the middle.
lines.caption: The middle side has to stay below seventeen, and the smallest below the middle.

lines.text: Longest side sixteen: the other two add to twenty. From five and fifteen up to nine and eleven.
lines.caption: Longest side sixteen: the other two add to twenty. From five and fifteen up to nine and eleven.

lines.text: That's five more.
lines.caption: That's five more.

lines.text: Longest fifteen: seven and fourteen, up to ten and eleven. That's four.
lines.caption: Longest fifteen: seven and fourteen, up to ten and eleven. That's four.

lines.text: Longest fourteen gives two. Longest thirteen gives just one: eleven, twelve, thirteen.
lines.caption: Longest fourteen gives two. Longest thirteen gives just one: eleven, twelve, thirteen.

lines.text: Longest twelve gives none. Two different sides below twelve add to at most twenty-one.
lines.caption: Longest twelve gives none. Two different sides below twelve add to at most twenty-one.

lines.text: Seven plus five plus four plus two plus one is nineteen. That's Choice B!
lines.caption: Seven plus five plus four plus two plus one is nineteen. That's Choice B!

lines.text: Here's another way. Count every triangle, then take away the ones with a repeated side.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Count every triangle, then take away the ones with a repeated side.

lines.text: Allow repeats, and the same list grows to twenty-seven triangles in all.
lines.caption: Allow repeats, and the same list grows to twenty-seven triangles in all.

lines.text: A triangle with a repeat has two equal sides. Call each one x.
lines.caption: A triangle with a repeat has two equal sides. Call each one x.

lines.text: So the third side is thirty-six minus two x.
lines.caption: So the third side is thirty-six minus two x.

lines.text: The third side must be more than zero, so x is less than eighteen.
lines.caption: The third side must be more than zero, so x is less than eighteen.

lines.text: And x plus x must beat the third side, so x is more than nine.
lines.caption: And x plus x must beat the third side, so x is more than nine.

lines.text: That's x from ten to seventeen: eight triangles.
lines.caption: That's x from ten to seventeen: eight triangles.

lines.text: Twelve, twelve, twelve is one of them, counted just once.
lines.caption: Twelve, twelve, twelve is one of them, counted just once.

lines.text: Twenty-seven minus eight is nineteen. Same answer!
lines.caption: Twenty-seven minus eight is nineteen. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the leftovers are easier to count than what you want.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the leftovers are easier to count than what you want.

lines.text: Now the traps. Choice D, twenty-seven, counts every triangle. It forgets to remove the repeats.
lines.caption: Now the traps. Choice D, twenty-seven, counts every triangle. It forgets to remove the repeats.

lines.text: Choice C, twenty, removes the repeats but forgets twelve, twelve, twelve.
lines.caption: Choice C, twenty, removes the repeats but forgets twelve, twelve, twelve.

lines.text: That's twenty-seven minus seven.
lines.caption: That's twenty-seven minus seven.

lines.text: Choice E, thirty-five, is too many. There are only twenty-seven triangles in all!
lines.caption: Choice E, thirty-five, is too many. There are only twenty-seven triangles in all!

lines.text: Choice A, seventeen, is what you'd get if you skipped a row of the list.
lines.caption: Choice A, seventeen, is what you'd get if you skipped a row of the list.

lines.text: For example, the two with longest side fourteen.
lines.caption: For example, the two with longest side fourteen.

lines.text: An organized list by longest side keeps every triangle, so we land on nineteen.
lines.caption: An organized list by longest side keeps every triangle, so we land on nineteen.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now the perimeter is twenty-four.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now the perimeter is twenty-four.

lines.text: How many triangles with whole-number sides and three different side lengths are there?
lines.caption: How many triangles with whole-number sides and three different side lengths are there?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The longest side must be less than twelve, and at least eight.
lines.caption: Let's check. The longest side must be less than twelve, and at least eight.

lines.text: Longest eleven: the other two add to thirteen.
lines.caption: Longest eleven: the other two add to thirteen.

lines.text: Three and ten, four and nine, five and eight, six and seven. Four!
lines.caption: Three and ten, four and nine, five and eight, six and seven. Four!

lines.text: Longest ten: five and nine, six and eight. That's two.
lines.caption: Longest ten: five and nine, six and eight. That's two.

lines.text: Longest nine: just seven and eight. And longest eight gives none.
lines.caption: Longest nine: just seven and eight. And longest eight gives none.

lines.text: Four plus two plus one is seven triangles!
lines.caption: Four plus two plus one is seven triangles!

lines.text: Check another way: twelve triangles in all, minus five with a repeat. Seven!
lines.caption: Check another way: twelve triangles in all, minus five with a repeat. Seven!

lines.text: If you got seven, terrific work!
lines.caption: If you got seven, terrific work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Fix the longest side. It's at least a third of the perimeter, and less than half.
lines.caption: Fix the longest side. It's at least a third of the perimeter, and less than half.

lines.text: Then list row by row. Or count them all, and subtract the repeats.
lines.caption: Then list row by row. Or count them all, and subtract the repeats.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
